title: Jatin-Lalit's Sons Debut as Film Composers with YRF's Alpha
excerpt: Rohansh and Abeer Pandit, sons of legendary Bollywood composer Lalit Pandit, scored the soundtrack for Yash Raj Films' spy thriller Alpha — their identity hidden until after release.
body:
• Rohansh Pandit and Abeer Pandit, sons of Jatin-Lalit's Lalit Pandit, composed the soundtrack for YRF's Alpha, starring Alia Bhatt and Sharvari.
  • The duo was credited simply as "Rohansh and Abeer" — audiences had no idea about their Jatin-Lalit connection until actor Viveck Vaswani revealed it on Facebook.
  • Alpha's album includes tracks like Massacre, Champagne, Haaniya, Agni, Vaar Vaar, and Shadows, released on July 3, 2026.
  • Jatin-Lalit scored four iconic YRF soundtracks including Dilwale Dulhania Le Jayenge and Mohabbatein before the duo split after Fanaa in 2006.

The next generation of one of Bollywood's most celebrated music families has arrived at the same studio where their father made history. Rohansh Pandit and Abeer Pandit — sons of Lalit Pandit, one half of the iconic composer duo Jatin-Lalit — made their film debut scoring the soundtrack for Yash Raj Films' Alpha, a spy thriller starring Alia Bhatt and Sharvari.

A Hidden Legacy

What makes the debut unusual is how long the connection stayed under wraps. The brothers were credited in the film simply as Rohansh and Abeer, with no surname. Audiences who watched Alpha and read the credits had no reason to connect them to Bollywood royalty, according to Bollywood Hungama.

The secret came out when actor-producer Viveck Vaswani posted a photograph on Facebook showing the brothers posing with their father Lalit Pandit at YRF's preview theatre. "It was a treat watching Alpha with the talented debut music director duo Rohansh Pandit and Abeer Pandit and their parents Meena Pandit and Lalit Pandit," Vaswani wrote. "The music is completely new age, sharp and sets tone for the high-octane action!"

"The music is completely new age, sharp and sets tone for the high-octane action!"

— Viveck Vaswani, Actor-Producer

The Soundtrack

Alpha's album, released on July 3, 2026, features seven tracks: Massacre, Champagne, Haaniya, Agni, Vaar Vaar, Shadows, and Rola Paen De. The brothers also composed themes for several key scenes in the film, including Hrithik Roshan's extended cameo sequence reprising his role as Kabir Dhaliwal from War 2. Lyrics were written by Kumaar, Anvita Dutt, Kausar Munir, and the brothers themselves. The film's background score was handled separately by Sanchit and Ankit Balhara.

This was not the brothers' first brush with the music industry. In 2023, as teenagers, they composed Coming Home, a peace anthem produced by Warner Bros. that drew early attention to their talent.

The Jatin-Lalit Legacy

Their father's shadow is considerable. Jatin-Lalit dominated Bollywood's music landscape through the 1990s and early 2000s, delivering soundtracks for Jo Jeeta Wohi Sikandar, Kuch Kuch Hota Hai, Kabhi Khushi Kabhie Gham, Dilwale Dulhania Le Jayenge, Mohabbatein, and Fanaa — the last four all for Yash Raj Films. Fanaa in 2006 was their final collaboration before the brothers split.

The fact that Rohansh and Abeer chose to debut with YRF — the same studio that produced their father's most iconic work — adds a layer of poetic symmetry. It also signals YRF's confidence in a new generation, handing them the music reins for one of the studio's marquee Spy Universe productions alongside established stars.

Industry Connections Debate

The revelation immediately triggered discussions on social media, according to BlazesTrends. Fans began dissecting the soundtrack for stylistic similarities to their father's work, while others debated the role of industry connections in Bollywood's most lucrative film franchises. The brothers' decision to drop their surname in the credits suggests an awareness of this dynamic — an attempt to let the work stand on its own before the lineage became part of the conversation.

Alpha features Alia Bhatt and Sharvari as leads, with Bobby Deol as the antagonist, Anil Kapoor, and Dia Mirza in a guest appearance. The film is part of YRF's Spy Universe and was directed with action sequences choreographed by Craig Macrae.
